question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP initialize request (jsonrpc 2.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, clientInfo public-agents-researcher 1.0), then a tools/list on the same session, Content-Type application/json, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

decoded.challenge: none: the 200 carries no www-authenticate header
decoded.tools-list: 200 with no session id issued: 3 tools (firecrawl_scrape, firecrawl_search, firecrawl_parse)
decoded.protected-resource-metadata: 404 with an empty body at https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v2/mcp (the RFC 9728 path for the resource; nothing named it)
decoded.authorization-server-metadata: not looked for: step 2 named no authorization server
decoded.rest: not measured today: the documented REST calls are POSTs (scrape, search), and the entry's 2026-09-09 note records them as 403 to a keyless cloud IP

finding: With no credentials, an MCP initialize POST to mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp answers 200 (firecrawl-fastmcp 3.24.1), and a tools/list answers 200 with three tools: firecrawl_scrape, firecrawl_search and firecrawl_parse. No challenge is sent and the RFC 9728 default path answers 404 with an empty body, so the server publishes no OAuth discovery; the vendor's documented path is an API key, which this probe does not carry. A keyless handshake and a keyless list say nothing about a keyless call, and the entry's 2026-09-09 note records the REST scrape and search endpoints answering 403 to this kind of IP; no tool was called today. Same 200 as that measurement; the three-tool list is recorded here for the first time. Nothing here measures what the server does with a key.
